To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reduced bioenergetic flux is present very early in AD and that the resulting protean retrograde response is likely to have both adaptive and deleterious consequences.
reduced bioenergetic flux and increased mitochondrial mass are present early in AD and that the mitochondrial fusion-fission balance shifts towards increased fission during AD progression.

reduced bioenergetic flux and altered mitochondrial mass and dynamics occur in AD and MCSI cybrid cell lines, that many of these changes are also present in AD subject brains and that reduced bioenergetics in MCI and AD is not brain-limted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the bioenergetics of AD.
understanding the bioenergetic dysfunction in AD, MCI and related conditions.
the molecular and biochemical mechanisms of Alzheimer's Disease (AD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
mitochondrial dysfunction is a key event in the development of AD and MCI.
the bioenergetic dysfunction in AD and MSCI is a consequence of mitochondrial dysfunction.
the AD and MCL cybrid models are useful in understanding the pathogenesis of AD and MCI and that they can be used as a platform to screen for potential therapeutic targets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
reduced mitochondrial function in AD and MCSI is not a consequence of a single mechanism but is the result of the interplay among multiple mechanisms that are not yet fully understood.
reduced bioenergetic flux is an early and central event that occurs during the progression from healthy to AD brain.
reduced bioenergetic flux in AD is associated with a shift in the mitochondrial fission/fusion balance towards fission, and this shift in the balance may have important implications for AD pathology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AD and MCI can be modeled in cell culture and the resulting cell lines are useful tools to investigate the pathobiology of these disorders.
the AD and MCL cybrid models are valuable tools for investigating the molecular mechanisms that contribute to the pathophysiology of AD and MCI.
the AD brain is a bioenergetic sink that is not limited to the brain.
